identification.summary: UNC6201 is a Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG)/Mandiant designation for a suspected PRC-nexus threat cluster [S1]. GTIG reported it exploiting CVE-2026-22769 (CVSS 10.0), hard-coded default credentials for the admin user of the Apache Tomcat Manager in Dell RecoverPoint for Virtual Machines, to upload a malicious WAR file and run commands as root [S1]. It deployed the SLAYSTYLE web shell, the BRICKSTORM backdoor and a newer C# backdoor, GRIMBOLT, and pivoted into VMware infrastructure using 'Ghost NICs' and iptables-based Single Packet Authorization [S1].
identification.firstObserved: GTIG: earliest identified exploitation of CVE-2026-22769 was mid-2024; in September 2025 Mandiant observed BRICKSTORM binaries on compromised appliances replaced with GRIMBOLT [S1].
identification.notes: GTIG states UNC6201 has 'notable overlaps' with UNC5221 (some secondary reports equate it with Silk Typhoon; the GTIG wording was not verified) but does not currently consider the two clusters the same [S1]. UNC5221 is the cluster GTIG linked to the BRICKSTORM campaign against US legal, SaaS, BPO and technology firms [S2]. Do not merge UNC6201 and UNC5221 facts. No Microsoft name is established in the sources gathered; treat the Silk Typhoon equivalence as unverified.

attribution.sponsor: GTIG describes UNC6201 only as a 'suspected PRC-nexus threat cluster'; no specific PRC agency or contractor is named in the source reviewed [S1].
attribution.confidence: Low-to-moderate as worded by GTIG: 'suspected' PRC nexus, with overlaps to UNC5221 but not considered the same cluster [S1]. No government attribution to UNC6201 was found; CISA/NSA/Canadian Cyber Centre report AR25-338A concerns PRC state-sponsored use of BRICKSTORM generally and was not reviewed in full [S3].
attribution.basis: GTIG/Mandiant incident response findings: shared C2 between BRICKSTORM and GRIMBOLT, tooling and VMware-focused tradecraft overlapping with UNC5221 [S1].

objectives: GTIG does not state UNC6201 objectives. Related BRICKSTORM reporting on UNC5221 assesses espionage against legal, SaaS, BPO and technology targets, including access to downstream customers and data useful for zero-day development; that is a different cluster and is context only [S2].

targeting.notes: GTIG's UNC6201 report does not give victim sectors, geographies or counts; it refers to 'affected organizations' with VMware infrastructure compromised [S1]. Reported BRICKSTORM targeting by UNC5221 (US legal, SaaS, BPO, technology) and by PRC actors per AR25-338A (government services and facilities, IT firms) is a related but separate cluster context [S2][S3][S4].

capabilities.summary: Exploitation of CVE-2026-22769 via authenticated WAR deployment to Tomcat Manager (/manager/text/deploy), then root command execution [S1]. SLAYSTYLE is a Java/JSP web shell that runs commands via /bin/sh -c [S1]. GRIMBOLT is a C# backdoor compiled with Native AOT and UPX-packed, giving remote shell and sharing C2 with BRICKSTORM; Native AOT strips CIL metadata, hindering static analysis [S1]. Persistence by modifying convert_hosts.sh, run at boot via rc.local [S1]. Lateral movement into VMware via temporary 'Ghost NIC' ports on ESXi VMs and an iptables Single Packet Authorization scheme on vCenter appliances: a hex string seen on port 443 whitelists the source IP, and for 300 seconds its port 443 traffic is redirected to port 10443 [S1]. Replacement of BRICKSTORM with GRIMBOLT was seen from September 2025; GTIG says it is unclear whether this was planned or a reaction to response efforts [S1].

diamond.adversary: Suspected PRC-nexus cluster UNC6201, with notable overlaps to UNC5221 but not judged the same by GTIG [S1].
diamond.capability: CVE-2026-22769 exploitation, SLAYSTYLE web shell, BRICKSTORM and GRIMBOLT backdoors, Ghost NICs, iptables Single Packet Authorization [S1].
diamond.infrastructure: GRIMBOLT C2 at wss://149.248.11.71/rest/apisession (IP 149.248.11.71), shared with BRICKSTORM; DNS-over-HTTPS use is a GTIG detection theme [S1].
diamond.victim: Unnamed 'affected organizations' running Dell RecoverPoint for Virtual Machines and VMware vCenter/ESXi; sectors not published [S1].
diamond.socioPolitical: Not stated for UNC6201; related UNC5221 BRICKSTORM reporting assesses national security and trade intelligence value and zero-day development [S2].
diamond.technology: Appliances and virtualization layers with limited EDR visibility: Dell RecoverPoint, VMware vCenter and ESXi [S1][S2].

gaps: Initial access vector was not confirmed by GTIG; UNC6201 is known to target edge appliances such as VPN concentrators [S1].
Victim sectors, regions and counts are not public in the GTIG report [S1].
Relationship to UNC5221/Silk Typhoon and to CrowdStrike's Warp Panda is unresolved; GTIG says the clusters are not currently considered the same [S1]. Microsoft naming not established.
Whether the GRIMBOLT swap was planned or reactive is unknown [S1].
Publication date appears as 2026-02-17 on the GTIG page fetched; some secondary results cite 2026-02-18.

Could not open: CISA AR25-338A full text, Dell advisory (kbdoc 000426773), and secondary articles from The Hacker News, Security Affairs and Truesec (fetch failures). Only search-result summaries were seen for [S2][S3][S4].
Objectives, sponsor agency and any government attribution of UNC6201 are unverified.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Backup and recovery appliances (Dell RecoverPoint) and VMware vCenter/ESXi hosts are key cyber terrain; compromise of them also undermines recovery [S1]. STEP 2: Environment is characterized by appliances with little or no EDR coverage [S1][S2]. STEP 3: Template is hard-coded credential abuse, then WAR web shell (SLAYSTYLE), then BRICKSTORM or GRIMBOLT, then Ghost NICs and SPA-gated vCenter proxying toward internal and SaaS networks [S1]. STEP 4: MLCOA is quiet long-dwell persistence in virtualization infrastructure for espionage (objective not stated by GTIG). MDCOA is use of access to backup systems to impair recovery during a crisis; this is inference not stated in the sources. Candidate indicators: any /manager requests in the RecoverPoint Tomcat audit log, new WARs under /var/lib/tomcat9, modified convert_hosts.sh, unexpected ESXi virtual NICs, iptables rules matching port 443/10443 redirection, traffic to 149.248.11.71 [S1].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: inventory RecoverPoint for VMs and vCenter instances on mission networks and confirm patched status per Dell's advisory [S1]. (2) Authorities: hunting on appliances and virtualization hosts may need system-owner and DODIN-operator coordination; confirm authorities before host-level collection. (3) Mission assurance: treat backup and recovery systems as mission-critical and protect restoration capability [S1]. (4) Coordination: share IOCs with DC3/DIB partners and track overlap with BRICKSTORM guidance in CISA AR25-338A [S3].

provenance.importedSummary: UNC6201 is a sophisticated Chinese state-sponsored hacking group that exploited CVE-2026–22769, a critical vulnerability in Dell RecoverPoint for Virtual Machines appliances, to establish a persistent presence. They deployed a permanent backdoor using techniques like Single Packet Authorization and "Port Knocking." Unlike typical hackers who conceal their activities within the Operating System, UNC6201 operated at the Virtualization Layer to avoid detection.
